items.citation:
# Citation

Candidate under formal verification; review pending.

## English

Erdős Problem JSP-000298 (Erdős Problem #360) investigates the minimum number of colors $f(n)$ required to color the integers $\{1, \dots, n-1\}$ such that no monochromatic subset sums to $n$. Originally posed by Erdős and Graham (1980), bounds of order $n^{1/3 \pm o(1)}$ were established by Noga Alon and Paul Erdős (*Acta Arithmetica* 74(3), 1996, pp. 269–272), with further sharp order bounds established by Conlon, Fox, and Pham (2021). This machine-checked Lean 4 candidate submission formalizes an elementary, constructive cubic-root upper bound: for all $n \ge 2, s \ge 1$ with $n \le s^3$, there exists an explicit coloring with $2s$ colors avoiding monochromatic subset sum $n$ (`exists_coloring_of_le_cube`), establishing $f(n) \le 2\lceil n^{1/3}\rceil$. The submission also formalizes the general interval avoidance theorem for any $k \ge 1$ (`interval_block_avoids_subset_sum`), modular divisibility avoidance (`dvd_subset_sum_free`), and the non-trivial lower bound $f(n) \ge 2$ for all $n \ge 3$ (`minColors_ge_two`).
items.recipients:
# Recipients

## English

Attribution for this formal candidate distinguishes the original mathematical proof from the machine-checked Lean 4 formalization:

1. RECIPIENT-JSP-000298-ALON: Noga Alon, co-author of the original mathematical proof establishing upper and lower bounds for monochromatic subset sum colorings (*Acta Arith.* 74 (1996), 269–272).
2. RECIPIENT-JSP-000298-ERDOS: Paul Erdős, who originally posed the problem and co-authored the 1996 resolution.
3. RECIPIENT-JSP-000298-SIXTIMENIGHT: Sixtimenight, author of the original machine-checked Lean 4 formalization, definitions, and verification package.

Formal proof authored by Sixtimenight. Candidate packaging and verification recorded by community curators and verifiers.

statement.text:
theorem exists_coloring_of_le_cube (n s : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hs : 1 ≤ s) (hns : n ≤ s ^ 3) :
    ∃ c : ℕ → Fin (2 * s), Erdos298.AvoidsMonoSubsetSum n (2 * s) c
statement.natural_language_source: Erdos Problem JSP-000298 (Erdos #360, Alon-Erdos 1996, Conlon-Fox-Pham 2021): Let n >= 2, s >= 1 with n <= s^3. There exists a coloring of {1, ..., n-1} with 2*s colors such that no monochromatic subset sums to n. This constructively establishes the elementary cubic-root chromatic upper bound f(n) <= 2*ceil(n^(1/3)) on subset-sum avoidance, alongside the non-trivial lower bound f(n) >= 2 for all n >= 3.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.HasSubsetSum
definitions_reviewed.review: Specifies existence of a subfinset T ⊆ S with sum equal to target n.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.AvoidsSubsetSum
definitions_reviewed.review: Negation of HasSubsetSum, asserting that no subfinset of S has sum equal to n.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.AvoidsMonoSubsetSum
definitions_reviewed.review: Asserts that every color class of coloring c on {1, ..., n-1} avoids subset sum n.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.intervalBlock
definitions_reviewed.review: Defines the large interval blocks A_k = {x ∈ {1, ..., n-1} | n ≤ (k+1)*x ∧ k*x < n}.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.smallRemainder
definitions_reviewed.review: Defines the small remainder set R = {x ∈ {1, ..., n-1} | (s+1)*x < n}.

definitions_reviewed.name: Erdos298.smallBlock
definitions_reviewed.review: Partitions remainder R into s blocks C_j = R ∩ [j*s, (j+1)*s - 1].
